Flux Data From July Point Correction Test.......................................................31 6 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The National Solar Thermal Test Facility (NSTTF) is a DOE Core Capability and Technology Deployment Center located in Albuquerque, NM. It is operated by Sandia National Laboratories (Sandia) for the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). The NSTTF is the only multi-mission, multi-use, multi-story test facility of its type in the United States. The NSTTF was founded in 1978 and began testing with high heat flux that same year. Over the past 45 years, the NSTTF has been at the forefront of the research, design, fabrication, and testing of many of the critical Solar Thermal Technologies. Over the four decades since our founding, the mission of the NSTTF has grown to include the development of thermal resistant materials, new thermal receiver technologies, like our generation 3 falling particle system, optical metrology techniques like SOFAST 2.0, molten salt testing, thermal energy storage, solar thermal chemistry, and more. We use this pedigree and experience to develop the thermal technologies of tomorrow. To accomplish these missions, the team at the NSTTF draws on the experience and expertise of our staff along with the world-class facilities at Sandia National Laboratories to further the science of solar thermal technologies in diverse applications. We remain a trusted partner for high-quality and impactful research in both fundamental and applied arenas.
